summary.headline: Orders jumped to 745, the highest in eight weeks, but revenue slipped slightly and the quarter remains behind target at 85.5%.

points.what: Orders reached 745, up 9.9% on the week and 58.5% on last year, above the 8-week average of 689 and outside the 8-week range.
points.so_what: Volume was the strongest in two months, yet 58.5% growth is still below the 75% growth the targets assume.

points.what: Gross revenue was $50,652, down 0.7% week on week and up 58.6% year on year, close to the 8-week average of $50,363.
points.so_what: Revenue did not follow the order gain, leaving the week at 91.3% of its $55,460 target.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 5.4 pp to 16.8%, the highest in the 8-week history, and is 0.6 pp above last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $609 of revenue in the week.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $201,573 against a target of $235,861, an attainment of 85.5% and a gap of $34,288.
points.so_what: Nine weeks remain in the quarter, with $572,982 still needed to reach the full-quarter target of $774,555.

points.what: The cancellation rate moved +5.4 pp to 16.8%, well above the 1.0 pp notable threshold and above every week in the 8-week history.
points.so_what: At roughly $609 of revenue per percentage point, this is the main reason order growth did not convert into revenue growth.

points.what: AOV fell 3.7% to $81.70, outside its 8-week range, though still 0.8% above last year's $81.03.
points.so_what: A lower value per order means each additional order contributes less revenue toward the weekly target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate is reported for the mature week of 05 Jan 2026, as the two most recent weeks are not yet mature.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week cannot be judged yet and will only be visible in about two weeks.

points.what: Orders hit 90.0% of the weekly target of 828 (a gap of 83 orders) and revenue hit 91.3% of the $55,460 target, a gap of $4,808.
points.so_what: Both measures are behind target, and next week's bar rises to 774 orders and $57,034 of revenue.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue of $201,573 is 85.5% of the $235,861 target to date, behind by $34,288, with January the only month reported and behind target.
points.so_what: The shortfall carried into the quarter is the same as the year-to-date shortfall, since the year is four weeks old.

points.what: Reaching the $3,888,802 full-year target needs $75,250 of revenue per week over the remaining 49 weeks, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $50,757.
points.so_what: The required pace is far above the current pace, so the full-year target is a stretch at this run-rate.

points.what: North America added 20 orders, 29.9% of the total weekly increase, reaching 172 orders, up 13.2% week on week and 72.0% year on year.
points.so_what: It was the largest regional contributor to the week's order gain, though its 72.0% year-on-year growth still sits under the 75% the targets assume.

points.what: All four regions grew, with LATAM up 17.6% to 120 orders (26.9% of the change) and EMEA up 14.8% to 132 orders (25.4%), while APAC rose 3.9% to 321.
points.so_what: Growth was broad rather than concentrated, but APAC, the largest region at 43.1% of orders, moved the least.

points.what: Search contributed 38 orders, 56.7% of the weekly increase, rising 7.9% to 519 orders, while Facebook grew 30.6% to 47 and Display 18.8% to 38.
points.so_what: Search, at 69.7% of all orders, remains the source that determines whether weekly volume meets target.

points.what: AOV fell 3.7% to $81.70 from $84.86, but remains 0.8% above last year's $81.03.
points.so_what: With orders up 9.9% and AOV down, revenue ended 0.7% lower on the week.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 5.4 pp to 16.8% and is 0.6 pp higher than the same week last year.
points.so_what: Both the weekly and yearly moves are unfavourable, and each percentage point equates to about $609 of revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 05 Jan 2026 was 11.2%, unchanged on the prior week but 0.7 pp above last year.
points.so_what: Return behaviour is stable week to week, though it sits slightly worse than the same period last year.

points.what: New customer signups reached 247, up 6.0% on the week and 20.5% on last year.
points.so_what: Signups are growing more slowly than orders, which rose 9.9% weekly and 58.5% yearly.
